mn83:7.4: When many thousand years had passed, the barber saw grey hairs growing on the head of King Maghadeva’s son.
mn83:7.5: He said to King Maghadeva’s son,
mn83:7.6: ‘The messengers of the gods have shown themselves to you.
mn83:7.7: Grey hairs can be seen growing on your head.’
mn83:7.8: ‘Well then, my dear barber, carefully pull them out with tweezers and place them in my cupped hands.’
mn83:7.9: ‘Yes, Your Majesty,’ replied the barber to King Maghadeva’s son. He carefully pulled out those grey hairs with tweezers and placed them in the cupped hands of King Maghadeva’s son.
mn83:8.1: King Maghadeva’s son gave the barber a prize village, then summoned the crown prince and said,
mn83:8.2: ‘Dear prince, the messengers of the gods have shown themselves to me.
mn83:8.3: Grey hairs can be seen growing on my head.
mn83:8.5: Now it is time to seek heavenly pleasures.
mn83:8.6: Come, dear prince, rule the realm.
mn83:8.7: I shall shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.
mn83:8.8: For dear prince, you too will one day see grey hairs growing on your head. When this happens, after giving a prize village to the barber and carefully instructing the crown prince in kingship, you should shave off your hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.
mn83:8.9: Keep up this good practice that I have founded. Do not be my final man.
mn83:8.10: When a pair of men are living, the one who breaks such good practice is their final man.
mn83:8.12: “Keep up this good practice that I have founded. Do not be my final man.”’
mn83:9.1: And so, after giving a prize village to the barber and carefully instructing the crown prince in kingship, King Maghadeva’s son shaved off his hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness here in this mango grove.
mn83:9.2: He meditated spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, he spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
mn83:9.3: He meditated spreading a heart full of compassion …
mn83:9.5: equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, he spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
mn83:9.6: For 84,000 years King Maghadeva’s son played games as a child, for 84,000 years he acted as viceroy, for 84,000 years he ruled the realm, and for 84,000 years he led the spiritual life after going forth here in this mango grove.

mn83:13.15: to have Nimi as their king. He is a just and principled king, a great king who stands by his duty.

mn83:13.17: And he observes the sabbath on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth of the fortnight.”
